title: Coasts and islands: four ways to read the water
description: Start with a group of islands, follow the sea into a glacier-shaped valley, meet an estuary and finish at a coral reef around a lagoon.
introduction:
A group of islands, a narrow sea inlet and a ring of reef can all catch your eye on a map. They have different names because the names describe different things.

Begin with the island group. Then follow the shape of the coast, the meeting of waters and the edge of a lagoon. Each reading stands on its own; short quizzes are optional.
prerequisites: No geography background needed. Each new term is explained in the reading.

lessons.objective: Identify the group without assuming that every island has the same origin.

lessons.level: 2 · Follow the sea into a valley
lessons.objective: Connect a fjord’s sea water and steep valley to earlier glacier erosion.
Explain brackish water and recognise that freshwater estuaries also exist.

lessons.level: 4 · Separate the reef from its lagoon
lessons.objective: Distinguish an atoll’s reef ring from the water it surrounds.

glossary.definition: A group or chain of islands.
A sea inlet occupying a steep-sided valley shaped by glaciers.
Partly salty, as in a mixture of freshwater and seawater.
A ring-shaped coral reef surrounding, or nearly surrounding, a lagoon.
Water partly separated from a larger body of water by a natural barrier.

outcomes: Identify the group without assuming that every island has the same origin.
Connect a fjord’s sea water and steep valley to earlier glacier erosion.
Explain brackish water and recognise that freshwater estuaries also exist.
Distinguish an atoll’s reef ring from the water it surrounds.
